call_points.text: Management expects to exceed 20% annual revenue and profit growth guidance, keeping conservative guidance publicly.
YouTube Shorts monetisation deal remains under negotiation and is expected to be completed in Q3 FY27.
Catalog content acquired three or more years ago contributes around 85% of company revenue, with recent content providing 15%.
H1FY27 total payout was ₹127.1 Cr including buyback, with a Q2FY27 interim dividend of ₹6.5 per share.
Shorts monetisation is expected to migrate from a fixed price model to share of advertising revenue.
Public performance rights revenue is expected to surpass ₹2,500-3,000 crore over the next five years.
Longer term, content spend is budgeted at 20-25% of revenue.
Digital contributed about 75% of revenue this quarter.
Only about 15% of revenue comes from songs released in the last three years.
Cash was about ₹345 Cr on 30 June 2026.
Last year's PAT of ₹217 Cr will be distributed this year as dividend and buyback.
Buyback board meeting moved to 5 August to also weigh an open-market buyback effective 1 August.
YouTube Shorts renewal still under negotiation; update by end of Q2.
Employee cost rose on moving consultants to payroll; quarterly run-rate expected to hold.
No promoter stake sale is planned or in the pipeline.
Company is searching for a replacement after Hari Nair's exit.
FY27 guidance is set at 20% top-line growth and 20% bottom-line growth.
Q4 employee cost rose 78% YoY due to annual increment provisions, with normal run-rates expected in Q1.
Total dividend distributed in FY26 reached ₹166 Cr.
Revenue mix for FY26 stood at 70% digital and 30% non-digital (publishing, public performance, brands).
YouTube Shorts views declined, but management sees no material revenue impact as long videos drive monetization.
Public performance industry is currently around ₹500 Cr and expected to grow to ₹3,000 Cr in 3 years.

operating_notes.text: Paid subscriptions contribute 10% to 15% of digital revenue, expanding at 30-40% CAGR.
YouTube subscriber base reached 153 million as of March 2026.
Released 66 new songs in Q4 FY26 (47 film and 19 non-film songs).
Q1FY27 released 73 songs (55 film, 18 non-film); cumulative YouTube subscribers 158.3 million.
Subscription is 10-15% of platform revenue in India versus over 50% globally; paid subscribers growing 40-50% CAGR.
About 15% of revenue comes from songs released in the last three years; content sourcing split one-third Tips Films, one-third outside producers, one-third non-film.
Acquisition/in-house music production cost was ₹12.13 Cr in Q2FY27 against ₹39.95 Cr in Q1FY27 and ₹5.79 Cr in Q2FY26.
Advertisement and sales promotion spend was ₹12.56 Cr in Q2FY27 against ₹3.43 Cr in Q1FY27.
The company has one reportable segment, Audio/video Products, and no subsidiaries.
Q2FY27: 73 songs released (40 film, 33 non-film); YouTube subscriber base 164.5 million, total views over 54.3 billion.
Q2FY27: Content investment increased 97% YoY compared to Q2FY26.
Q2FY27: Share buyback of ₹44.44 crore completed during the quarter.
Q2FY27: 73 new songs released; catalogue over 38,000 songs across 25+ languages.
Q2FY27: YouTube subscribers 164.5 million; quarterly views 54.3 billion.
H1FY27: total payout ₹127.1 Cr including buyback; Q2FY27 interim dividend ₹6.5 per share.
Catalog content older than 3 years contributes roughly 85% of revenue, while content acquired within the last 3 years contributes 15%.
Warner Music partnership accounts for 25% to 30% of revenue and is scheduled for renewal in FY28.
The company writes off 100% of content costs in the same quarter/year it releases the music.
